title: The Myth of Restrictive Working-Time Agreements: Firms' Working-Time Adjustment after Exit from Collective Bargaining
abstract: arXiv:2610.12049v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Employers in Germany argue that collective agreements restrict their flexibility concerning working hours. Using data from the IAB Establishment Panel for the years 2008 to 2024, we investigate working-time adjustments after exit from collective bargaining. We find that exit is associated with only a modest increase in weekly working hours of around 0.3 to 0.6 per cent using fixed-effects and event-study models, corresponding to eight to thirteen additional minutes per week. This adjustment occurs shortly after leaving collective bargaining coverage. We further find no evidence that other margins of working-time adjustment, such as Saturday or Sunday work, are used more extensively after exit. In contrast to previous survey evidence, our findings call into question that working-hours constraints are one of the main drivers of exit from collective bargaining coverage.

translated_title: 限制性工作时间协议的迷思：企业退出集体谈判后的工作时间调整
translated_abstract: 德国雇主认为集体协议限制了他们在工作时间方面的灵活性。利用2008年至2024年的IAB企业面板数据，我们研究了企业退出集体谈判后的工作时间调整情况。通过固定效应模型和事件研究模型，我们发现退出集体谈判仅与每周工作时间约0.3%至0.6%的温和增长相关，相当于每周增加8至13分钟。这一调整发生在企业脱离集体谈判覆盖范围后不久。我们进一步发现，没有证据表明退出后其他工作时间调整渠道（如周六或周日工作）被更广泛地使用。与以往调查证据相反，我们的研究结果对“工作时间限制是促使企业退出集体谈判覆盖范围的主要驱动因素之一”这一观点提出了质疑。
tldr: 利用德国2008至2024年企业面板数据的研究发现，企业退出集体谈判后每周工作时间仅增加约0.3%至0.6%（8至13分钟），其他工作时间调整渠道也无显著变化，这一结果质疑了工作时间限制是退出集体谈判主要驱动因素的传统观点。
en_tdlr: Using German establishment panel data from 2008 to 2024, this study finds that exiting collective bargaining is associated with only a modest increase in weekly working hours of 0.3 to 0.6 per cent (eight to thirteen minutes), challenging the claim that working-hours constraints are a main driver of firms' exit from collective bargaining coverage.
